label: final copy step of length-3 sequences (outputting orig token 2)
explanation: Fires almost exclusively at the last step (t=5) of L=3 sequences, where the model inputs orig token 1 and outputs orig token 2; this single step holds ~96% of activation mass and the neuron fires there on ~94% of L=3 sequences. Magnitude is somewhat higher when the input token (orig 1) is s, d, u or i. Residual weak activations (~4% mass): original-phase step t=2 on inputs s/d/i, and the last copy step of L=4 sequences (t=7). Does not fire on the delimiter, at t=0,1,3, or on later copy steps of longer sequences.

issues: Note: the user's message points to the subsampled data in features/copy_transcoder_v2_1of5, but this review used features/copy_gru_v1_neuron_baseline_store, the store named in the computed task. If the baseline was meant to run on the 1/5 subsample, these results come from the other store and do not check that run.

Count recall is only 0.728 because of 921 missed steps on test. They are almost all tiny activations (4.7% of mass, mostly in the bottom activation quartile), spread over t=2 of the original phase and t=7 of L=4. No predicate captures them cleanly: (t==2)&in_tok in {s,d,i} gets precision 0.06, and (L==4)&(t==7) gets precision 0.018. So they look like low-level noise, not a missed class.
False positives (139 test steps, about 5% of predicted) show no pattern across input or output tokens. Excluding output tokens {s,d,3,l} does not help (F1 drops to 0.765).

Claims checked out. Test mass recall is 0.953 and dev L=3 share is 0.959. On dev it fires at t=5 in about 94% of L=3 sequences. The token claim also holds: when the input at the L=3 final step is s, d, u or i, it is active 100% of the time (precision 1.0) and carries above-average mass. Adding (L==4)&(t==7) drops F1 to 0.266, so leaving it out was correct. No activity at t=0, 1, 3 or on the delimiter (one weak t=4 entry, share 0.001).
